project_metadata.job_title: Senior Full-Stack / Platform Engineer for AI SaaS Platform
project_metadata.job_description:
We are building a confidential AI SaaS platform and need a hands-on senior technical operator who can learn quickly, hit the ground running, and help us move faster without breaking production quality.
This is not a junior role, not an agency role, and not a theory-only architecture role. We need someone who can open a complex repo, understand what matters, identify risk, fix real issues, improve tests, and help ship safely.
You will work directly with the founder on a fast-moving AI SaaS product with active frontend, backend, infrastructure, security, integration, and release-quality workstreams.
The ideal candidate has a strong track record of joining complex products, learning quickly, and becoming useful within days, not months.
The first engagement will likely involve reviewing active PRs, resolving CI failures, fixing security/dependency issues, improving frontend/backend reliability, reducing Dev/Prod risk, and helping stabilise release quality.
You must be evidence-driven. Every change needs clear proof: what changed, what was tested, what risk remains, and whether the work is safe to merge.
NDA required before detailed access is provided.

Thank you for today’s productive conversation and for explaining the vision to me.

I’ve put together some questions for Angeli before our session and am sharing them now so she has time to review them beforehand:

Grounding and governors

What mechanism currently enforces source-grounding?
Are the governors implemented in code or through prompt instructions, and where are they located in the repo?

Release 1 readiness recommendation

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], I have three scope questions arising from the front-end review. These are product decisions rather than defects, so they need your input rather than Anjali’s.

1. Does the multi-user scenario belong in Release 1? The functionality for sending an invite exists, but the front end does not call POST /account/users/accept, and there is no route for the invitation link, leaving invited users with nowhere to land. Completing the flow end-to-end would also require backend functionality for the member-list, revoke and remove actions, and none of those endpoints currently exist.

2. The product description promises "Instant access revocation", but while #1427 remains open, the disconnect endpoints report success without deleting the connection record. The front end handles this properly by refusing to report success, which means the current behaviour does not match the claim.

3. Anjali’s requirements for per-member metering—token consumption per member, usage breakdown and individual limits—are available only in the superadmin console under /admin. Account owners cannot access any of these features. Was an owner-facing view intended for R1, or does it belong to Phase 2?
